prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot on request), Main Transformer, export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere). Public grid, port ops out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; blocks protection-conflicting commands; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode if aux lost), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image; repeat pass if coverage insufficient). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (trends/alarms escalated to Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, station service transformers, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling, sheds nonessential, start-failure alarm, UPS; produces Start Test Trace in functional test). Substation Operator: keeps limits, follows switching instructions; shift review of alarms/restrictions/handover; rounds; checks transformer temps/cooling/oil, relay state, permits, access records, fire panel, generator fuel/battery. Grid Dispatcher sets dispatch; Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard) allocates output, assigns vessel/crew after Duty Planner confirms. Frequency response only in authorized mode; comms loss keeps local protection; alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; work packages; Session Revocation Receipt; forwards observations to Shore Control Room (Amber Quay): escalates alerts, retains decisions, permit/isolation/test/restoration records), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale), Operations Radio Console, Work Permit Portal (blocks permit release until reviews/isolation refs complete), Personnel Tracking Console. Control Engineer validates data (stale=unverified), investigates SCADA/local discrepancies before reliance, confirms restored state checks. Duty Planner ranks, submits scope/crew/window, coordinates revised windows, closes authorization after Field Supervisor confirms completion. Weather Service, Metocean Buoy; Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record). Modes: Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Vessel Master gets Transfer Manifest Addendum; Quiet Harbor blocks route change. Crew Transfer Vessel: Harness Audit Card (HSE Officer). Port Agent: Berth Slot Confirmation. Storekeeper validates Backorder Exception Slip from Warehouse System (Mosslight). Permits: Field Supervisor pauses/reassesses on change, confirms clear before isolation removal; Electrical Technician identifies isolations, reports defects;

New part:
S355: Foxglove is exercised under the approved test procedure to confirm reliable backup starting and stable output.
S356: The operator records test results and raises a defect promptly if the Emergency Generator fails to start or sustain its required load.
S357: The Cybersecurity Gateway uses the revocation receipt to support access control during routine account and session reviews.
S358: Switching is performed only by authorized personnel using approved instructions and positive confirmation of equipment identity.
S359: Before operating a breaker or isolator, the operator verifies the required clearances and confirms that affected parties are informed.
S360: If a protection alarm, abnormal electrical condition, or loss of critical monitoring occurs, the operator limits further switching and escalates the condition.
S361: The operator places the Offshore Substation in Substation Degraded when required by operating procedures and communicates the resulting restrictions.
S362: The Grid Dispatcher is notified when a condition could affect export capability or compliance with grid instructions.
S363: The Electrical Technician supports fault diagnosis and maintenance under the applicable work authorization and isolation controls.
S364: The Shore Control Room receives concise status updates, including operating limitations and the expected time of the next review.
S365: Shift records capture inspections, alarms, tests, switching actions, defects, and handover items so that decisions remain traceable.
S366: Grid export is coordinated against the dispatch instructions, equipment capability, and the agreed operating limits for the connection.
S367: Grid Dispatcher issues active-power targets and ramp instructions through the established dispatch channel.
S368: Control Engineer reviews each instruction for consistency with current plant status before applying it.
S369: SCADA Gateway provides the operational measurements used to track delivered power and instruction response.
S370: Fleet Dispatch Console compares the requested output with available turbine capability and known operating restrictions.
S371: The Shore Control Room maintains the current dispatch target, ramp rate, and next review time in the shift record.
S372: Grid Interface Relay produces an Export Limit Advisory when available export capability falls below the active dispatch target.
S373: Wildmere applies the accepted export ceiling to control outputs and records its effective time for audit.
S374: Shore Control Room uses the tap snapshot to check the recorded transformer position during export reviews.
S375: Control Engineer confirms that the control response follows the instruction and remains within the permitted ramp rate.
S376: When a Grid Constraint is active, the operator records its scope, start time, and expected review point.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
